Project_Ti: Pilot Project to Improve Soils at Villanueva Fields
Practices: No-till; subsoil plowing
Project_Su:
Transform dirt to healthy, regenerating soil on 6 acequia-irrigated acres with low fertility, so that food and cover crops grow sucessfully, and vigor and diversity improve, via these three objectives: 1. Improve my long-term soil improvement plan by working with soil health consultants to diagnose problems and refine farm practices to keep living roots in the soil and maximize soil and plant biodiversity. This will improve my ability to keep soil covered.
2. Purchase and/or contract equipment to help jumpstart soil improvement to address compaction that is inhibiting the establishment of roots by using a subsoil plow on 2 acres and address poor plant diversity by using a no-till drill on 5 acres (1 acre overlap).
3. Enrich the local agricultural community by involving neighbors and youth in the process of learning to improve area soils, so the community has more diverse and current models long-term agricultural, economic and biological success and diversity.
Creator: NMSU_SparcLab

Project_Ti: Reduced tillage with permanent raised bed establishment and living mulch trial to improve soil health in furrow irrigated specialty crop production.
Practices: Diverse cover crop; conservation tillage; living mulch; pollinator habitat
Project_Su: During the 2020 production season, a pilot study will be conducted to 1) establish reduced tillage, permanent raised bed production (PRB) research sites and 2) select living mulch cultivars that provide a) nutrients, cover, and a living root to normally exposed soil, b) a floral resource for pollinators, and c) act as a secondary crop for producers. The combination of these practices will reduce erosion and the impact of furrow irrigation on soil health and structure.

Project_Ti: Using Cover Crops/Livestock/Adaptive Grazing to Restore Soil Health
Practices: Diverse cover crop; no-till; rotational grazing; rangeland grass restoration
Project_Su: This project will address an old alfalfa/brome hay field (South Hayward Field) that was farmed/hayed for decades, beginning in the 1930’s. The 360 acres has not been irrigated since 2008. The drought and lack of irrigation caused this field to decline rapidly in the last 10 years with over 50% bare ground on parts of the farmed areas of this 748-acre field. Planting a diverse cover crop with a no-till drill in the spring of 2020, applying high-intensity adaptive grazing with cattle during the growing season will significantly speed up the process of re-establishing armor/cover on the field to improve soil health.

Planting a perennial crop would reduce soil distubance and provide year round soil coverage. The importance of this would be to recude the current loss of top soil to high winds. The second objective is to reduce water waste by lining a dirt irrigation ditch and reservoir that is currently being used on the farm.

Project_Ti: Rio Fernando Park: Regenerative Agriculture Restoration Project
Practices: Diverse cover crop; no-till; compost application; pollinator habitat

Specifically, we will plant 6 acres with rye, wheat, and barley using a no-till seeder; the remaining 2 acres will be planted as native pollinator habitat. All 8 acres will be flood-irrigated and treated with soil amendments; high-quality compost created on the property will be spread as compost extract to further encourage microbial health.

Project_Ti: Berm & Swale "HugelKeltur" Runoff Catchment Food Forest

Project_Su: I intend to use a German method of growing called "hugelkultur", in which logs, brush, and mulch are buried and covered with soil to create growing mounds with rich organic matter interiors. In New Mexico, I have adapted this method to be more subterranean and in a floodirrigated system because of our arid climate. I have found that this method works well to keep the soil covered, minimize soil disturbance on cropland, maximize biodiversity, and maintain a living root. I will also plant a food forest and local cover crops to maximize the efforts of regenerating the soil.
